claim: The romaji for 宇宙飛行士 runs its two words together, unlike the deck's other two-word compounds, which makes the longest reading in the unit harder to sound out.
evidence: 宇宙飛行士 back: 'Answer: Astronaut / Says: uchūhikōshi'. Compare 天気予報 'Says: tenki yohō' (Lesson 8), 短期大学 'Says: tanki daigaku' (Lesson 6), スポーツ選手 'Says: supōtsu senshu' (this unit).
fix: Split the romaji at the word boundary: 'uchū hikōshi'.
verdictReason: cards.json has pronunciation 'uchūhikōshi'. Of the collection's 19 shipping compounds of four or more kanji, 15 split at the morpheme boundary (tenki yohō, tanki daigaku, shiritsu daigaku, kōsei busshitsu, jidō hanbaiki, kippu uriba, tennō tanjōbi ...) and only four fuse (seikeigeka, sanfujinka, joshigakusei, kōtōgakkō); the romaji style spec's word-segmentation rule asks for words, not fused tokens. 'uchū hikōshi' matches the deck's own majority convention. Polish is the right weight: the reading is correct, only its spacing is off.

evidence: Card r-df96a6e9ec65: target 味, english 'Meaning; taste', reviewNote 'meaning and readings from KANJIDIC2'. KANJIDIC2 gives 味 only 'flavor, taste'. The same unit cards r-2353efbc3e76 意味 'Meaning', from the book's classroom vocabulary '意味 meaning'.
verdictReason: Checked src/reading/data/kanjidic2-compact.json: 味 has meanings ['flavor','taste'] and nothing else, so the card's own cited source does not support 'Meaning'. The book prints 味 in this lesson only inside 意味 (Useful Expressions vocabulary), and r-2353efbc3e76 意味 ships in the same unit with english 'Meaning'. docs/card-rules-reading.md rule 9 says a character's English is never the meaning of a word it appears in. Should-fix stands: the card teaches the learner a sense 味 does not have.

claim: The character card for 宇 gives the meaning of the word 宇宙 (universe) rather than of the character.
evidence: Card r-1832f9e9d247: target 宇, english 'Universe'. KANJIDIC2 gives 宇 'eaves, roof, house, heaven'. The book prints it only inside うちゅうひこうし（宇宙飛行士）astronaut; its partner card r-b71b26a524e8 宙 is 'Space; mid-air'.
fix: Change the English to something like 'Eaves; heaven (as in universe)' so it is the character's own meaning.
verdictReason: Checked kanjidic2-compact.json: 宇 has meanings ['eaves','roof','house','heaven']; 'Universe' is not among them and is the gloss of the word 宇宙, exactly the 将/将来 case rule 9 forbids. The card's reviewNote claims KANJIDIC2 as its source, so the content and its provenance disagree. The book prints 宇 only inside 宇宙飛行士 in this lesson. Polish is right: 'heaven' is close enough that the learner is misled rather than taught something false.
